notes: VERDICT PASS. Single attempt, no retries needed, so the 'never retry a create that may have partially succeeded without first checking the project list' constraint never came into play. BLAST RADIUS / CLEANUP: confirmed BEFORE creating, via searchCapability(entity=project, mode=destructive) returning zero matches, that no delete-project capability exists anywhere in this profile — matching create_project's own describeCapability guidance verbatim ('There is no delete-project capability in this index, so a project created by mistake cannot be removed through the registry — only through the UI'). The project created by this probe (id 379339429 / PR-2011) is therefore NOT removable through any capability in this profile; it can only be deleted via the TM UI. This is a bigger/worse version of the create_configuration finding: a configuration at least only pollutes a shared pool other projects read from, whereas an orphaned top-level project stays visible to the whole group (3452) indefinitely with no registry-level cleanup path at all. BOTH ID FORMS: the create response returns BOTH forms in a single call — data.project.id (379339429, integer, v1 form) and data.project.identifier (PR-2011, v2 form), plus thProjectId which duplicates id. No second call is needed to obtain either form, unlike the risk the campaign has been flagging elsewhere. CONTRACT: the 200 response matches its declared schema exactly — every returned key in data.project is declared, and nothing declared is missing except user_role and permissions, which the schema explicitly documents as conditional ('present only when the caller holds an explicit role here... a user whose access is implicit, such as through workspace ownership, gets neither this nor permissions') — their absence here is the documented behavior, not drift, so declared_missing is empty rather than listing them. TWO-SERIALIZER CHECK (against the create_root_folder defect on record): create_root_folder's data.project object is missing test_cases_count, test_runs_count, links and project_creator, and carries 16 undeclared fields (group_id, user_id, slug, is_demo, publicly_readable, access, applicable_role_id, applicable_role, four *_build_updated_at, source, archived, team_id, default_team_id, sub_group_id). This create_project response's data.project object has NONE of that: test_cases_count, test_runs_count and links are all present and correctly populated, and none of the 16 undeclared create_root_folder fields appear here at all. The two capabilities return visibly different project representations for what is nominally the same underlying record — confirming there are two distinct project serializers in play (one clean and schema-accurate, used by create_project and presumably the v1 project-detail read it shares its envelope with; one cut-down and leaking internal columns, used by create_root_folder's embedded project object) rather than one serializer with incidental per-endpoint drift. That is the more important finding than either endpoint's drift taken alone. ENTITLEMENT GATE: not applicable — response was an ordinary 200 with data.success:true, no {success:false} refusal-wearing-200 pattern observed. ERROR ENVELOPE: not exercised — the single attempt succeeded, so no error body was diffed against the success schema.
